purpose: Test whether the ~50% recovery fraction is suffix-content-specific or a general property of any additional processing step. Discriminates between: (a) any token helps (computation hypothesis), (b) any neutral token helps (neutral-processing hypothesis), (c) only specific tokens help (content-specific hypothesis).

predictions.H_computation: All suffixes (including bare newline) produce similar recovery fractions (~0.5). The mechanism is about extra computation, not content.
predictions.H_neutral: All neutral suffixes (comment, pass, newline) produce similar recovery; self-assign differs. The mechanism is about neutral processing.
predictions.H_content: Recovery fraction varies significantly across suffix types. The mechanism is content-specific.
predictions.H_comment_specific: Only comment-type suffixes produce the ~50% recovery. Comments trigger a specific attention pattern.
predictions.decisive_comparison: bare_newline vs comment_nochanges at d4. If recovery fractions within 5pp of each other, H_computation supported. If bare_newline recovery < 25%, H_content supported.

estimated_calls: 27 cells × 4 depths × 6 suffixes = 648 calls, ~4 min on Qwen3 CPU
